column1: # THE source-format route table — what kind of thing each file extension is, and which
# WHY THIS EXISTS (2026-09-02, a VBA-to-Mendix migration). The Stage 0 inventory in
# bin/source-sufficiency.sh listed source files by an extension ALLOWLIST. It had no .pptx,
# no .cls, no .bas. A 25-slide functional description with 22 diagrams sat in source/ for
# two months while BRDs, blueprint, build plan and module briefs were derived from the VBA
# exports alone — and the intake answer that closed the question said the deck "was already
# used by the triage pass", which nothing checked. The script's own comments record the same
# allowlist bug twice before (.yaml on 08-19, code on 08-31). Three misses, one shape: a
# coverage instrument that cannot see a file reports a corpus that never contained it.
# So the inventory is now EVERY file under the source root minus a short prune list, and this
# table says what each one is. An extension not listed here is NOT skipped — it is inventoried
# as `kind: unknown` and needs a disposition at Stage 1 like everything else. "Anything could
# be a source" (the user's words); the pipeline's answer to an unknown shape is a custom
# extractor per skills/extractor-quality-loop.md, or a waiver with a reason — never silence.
# Read by bin/source-sufficiency.sh (init: stamps `format`/`route` on each inventory row) and
# bin/source-ledger.sh (check: knows which formats carry embedded media that a text-only
# Format: TAB-separated, five columns. Blank lines and #-comments ignored. Extensions are
# lowercase without the dot; several per row, |-separated.
#   2 kind      docs | code | data | ui | contract | schema | media | archive | mail | diagram
#               — the same vocabulary the inventory's `kind` field takes (plus schema/media/
#               archive/mail/diagram, which the rubric readme lists as sub-kinds of the first six)
#   3 route     the extraction route that consumes it whole
#   4 media     yes if the container can hold embedded images/diagrams that text extraction
#               drops (Office/OpenDocument zips, PDFs). The ledger requires such a file's
#               disposition to account for its media count, not only its text.
#   5 notes     what "consumed" means for this format — the bar a disposition has to clear

column3: route
column5: notes

column5: A deck's diagrams are usually where the process shape is drawn; slide text alone is not the deck. Count from ppt/media/ inside the zip.

column5: Legacy binary; no direct reader in the toolkit. Conversion is part of the disposition.

column5: xl/media/ rarely matters; hidden sheets and named ranges do. State the sheet count in the disposition.

column3: convert to .xlsx first, then as xlsx
column5: Legacy binary.

column3: rows; header row is the schema
column5: One file, one table. Encoding and delimiter stated.

column5: A scanned PDF has no text layer; a text-only extraction returns nothing and reads as "empty document".

column3: read whole
text + tables + form fields (screens exported as HTML are UI evidence, not prose)
column5: An HTML export of a legacy screen is `ui`, not `docs` — reclassify by content.

column3: parse; schema and element names are structure
column5: A .xml can be anything (OutSystems export, config, data). Reclassify by content.

column3: parse; an OpenAPI/GraphQL contract grades as structure
tables, columns, keys, constraints → domain model input
column5: Frequently the best-specified thing in the corpus.

column3: RESTORE into a container (SQL Server / Oracle / Postgres image), then query: schema, row counts per table, and every configuration table the code reads. Highest-ranked source in the corpus when present (skills/query-the-model.md → evidence hierarchy)
column5: A production backup is production data: it outranks the code, the documents and every earlier conclusion. "Unrecoverable" is a claim to retest, not a finding — one project carried it for five months while a .bak sat in the folder; restored in an afternoon, it overturned five architecture decisions.

column3: schema + data via mdbtools / ODBC; forms, queries, macros and VBA modules are code
column5: An Access file is a whole app: schema, data, UI and logic in one container. The disposition names all four.

column3: schema + data
Path A code extraction (VBA/VB6): modules, procedures, form controls, event handlers
column5: .frm carries form layout (UI) as well as code; .cls with WORKBOOK/SHEET headers is Excel-hosted.
